newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks lower costs for nuclear arsenal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks lower costs for nuclear arsenal.

text.p: The Clinton administration is considering altering the mix of nuclear warheads on bombers, submarines and missiles so the arsenal's size can be maintained at lower cost, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.

One option under review by the Joint Chiefs of Staff would cut the number of deployed U.S. ballistic missile submarines and increase the number of warheads based on cheaper but more vulnerable land-based missiles and strategic bombers, the newspaper said, quoting senior U.S. officials.

The changes would help lower the $10 billion cost over the next five years of maintaining the nation's stockpile of more than 10,000 warheads, of which 6,000 are currently deployed. At the same time, it would also help fend off growing pressure to cut costs by undertaking new nuclear reductions.
Two expert panels have recently advised the Defence Department to trim costs and enhance U.S. security by scrapping additional weapons soon.

The administration has resisted these calls in part because defence officials are still reluctant to give up these weapons. The administration also promised Congress and told Russian leaders last year that it would not reduce the size of its nuclear arsenal below the existing level until the Russian legislature ratifies the 1993 START II treaty, which sets a ceiling of 3,500 nuclear warheads.
A White House official said the Pentagon now was seeking some greater flexibility to keep pressure on the Duma and save money.
